## Scope

Unit brief (read it; it quotes the owner): /home/ubuntu/Coding/missions/missions/fleet-refit/briefs/spaces-rail-brief.md. Builder proof: /home/ubuntu/Coding/missions/missions/fleet-refit/artifacts/spaces-rail/. Diff `git diff 7b4be199 ece9867f` (32 source/test files +1480/−298, plus rebuilt dist).

Builder's stated decisions (judge each): turn-end marker = `${agent_session}:${context_used}` counted only while bus_status=listening (context_used folded server-side from transcript vitals); never-seen agents seeded at their current turn once a board loads; mid-turn view keeps the old marker; viewing = active panel of a visible group + document visible, 1000ms dwell; blur cancels the switcher, a non-alt keydown while holding commits; stores herder.web.read-markers.v1 (cap 400 LRU) and herder.web.spaces.mru.v1 (cap 64) with .last-good backups via a shared browserRecord helper; spaceOverflowModel deleted.

## Verify

1. The unread signal is honest: a finished turn reliably becomes unread (can context_used stay equal across a real turn — e.g. a tiny turn, rounding, compaction lowering it back to a seen value, a missing/zero value?), no false unread on reload/reconnect/stream gaps, blocked always shows, retired/unknown never count. Check against the real /api/fleet payload shape (GET :4400/api/fleet is allowed) and the Go side that computes context_used.
2. Per-space derivation of open agent panels is correct for the active (live dockview) and inactive (stored layout) spaces, including a panel moved between spaces, a closed panel, a deleted/reopened space, and legacy mode.

5. Tests assert behaviour; source guards red when wiring is removed (verify at least one yourself). Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:check`; committed dist equals a fresh build.
6. Simplicity and readability weigh as much as correctness. Is the shared browserRecord helper, the LRU caps, the seeding, or any model earning its keep? Name concrete cuts if so.

deliveries.text:
# REQUEST-CHANGES — spaces-rail ece9867f

Reviewed `7b4be199..ece9867f`: 32 source/test files, +1480/−298, plus rebuilt dist. Work was performed in `/tmp/spaces-rail-review.WfuKwh`, a private `git archive` copy. The unit worktree remained clean and read-only. Only GET was used against :4400. Browser checks used a newly built archive binary on :4499 with isolated state; the serve was stopped by its PID afterward.

## Findings

1. **HIGH / P1 — Context usage is not a reliable completed-turn identifier.** `tools/herder/web/src/features/spaces/spaceAttentionModel.ts:36–44` treats equality of session and `context_used` as equality of completed turns. The Go implementation provides an input-token gauge: Claude sums input/cache-input counts (`internal/claudesession/read.go:211–226`); Codex uses `last_token_usage.input_tokens` (`internal/codexsession/read.go:186–205`). Neither supplies a completion identity or monotonic counter. Missing observer vitals produce no marker at all, and zero is omitted by the JSON tags (`internal/fleetview/fleet.go:28,272`). The observer only tracks Claude/Codex sessions (`internal/observer/discover.go:25`), so a listening row without those vitals can never become unread. A controlled browser sequence `listening(sa:1000) → active(sa:1000) → listening(sa:1000)` remains read despite the completed status transition. Equal counts can also recur after context reduction; raw counts are not rounded, so ordinary display rounding is not the concern. **Required:** establish a durable, placement-independent completion signal and its availability contract. Per the unit brief, if the existing payload cannot provide that, bring the signal decision back to line before expanding into Go. Do not claim that every finished turn changes this gauge. Evidence: `model-edge-cases.json`, `browser-adversarial.json` → `same-token-finished-turn`, and the Go locations above. The equal-count transition is a fixture test, not a claim that I triggered or observed such a turn in a live agent.

2. **MEDIUM / P2 — Late vitals fabricate an unread turn on first load.** `spaceAttentionModel.ts:60–66` seeds `''` whenever a row exists without a fingerprint, including an already-listening agent whose observer vitals are temporarily missing. When its unchanged historical context count arrives, `agentAttention` compares it against `''` and lights the badge. Browser reproduction: open listening eko with `context_used` absent, leave its panel hidden, then publish the same listening row with `context_used:5000`; the space changes from no waiting agents to one without any new turn. **Required:** distinguish an unknown baseline from a known pre-completion state; seed a late first valid marker without announcing a new completion unless completion evidence exists. Evidence: `browser-adversarial.json` → `no-vitals-seed` and `late-vitals-no-turn`; `false-unread.png`.

3. **MEDIUM / P2 — Moving a listening agent into/out of placement changes its read identity.** `spaceAttentionModel.ts:38` casts every `Row` to `Pane` and includes `agent_session`. That field exists on placed `Pane`, but not the Go `Row` used for unplaced/nested agents (`internal/fleetview/fleet.go:19–29,256–273`). Merely unplacing a read agent changes `sa:1000` to `:1000` and produces an unread badge; placing it again can produce the reverse error after a view. The stored marker must follow the agent, not placement availability. **Required:** use an identity present consistently across row variants as part of the corrected completion signal; add a placed/unplaced transition test. Evidence: `browser-adversarial.json` → `placement-only-change` and `model-edge-cases.json`. The live GET confirms placed payload shape; the unplaced case was constructed to match the Go row schema (the live snapshot had no unplaced agents).

4. **MEDIUM / P2 — Keyboard selection disappears below the scrollable switcher.** `tools/herder/web/src/features/spaces/SpaceSwitcher.tsx:22–38` changes the highlighted option but never scrolls it into view. At the supported 16-space limit on a 1440×900 viewport, cycling to index 14 leaves `scrollTop=0`; the selected row is at y=695–725 while the list ends at y=660. No selection is visible, but releasing Alt still switches to that unseen row. **Required:** keep the highlighted option within the list viewport on reveal and each index change. Evidence: `browser-adversarial.json` → `long-switcher-highlight`, `offscreen-selection.png`.

5. **MEDIUM / P2 — Held switcher leaks shell shortcuts to the underlying workspace.** `tools/herder/web/src/features/layout/shellShortcuts.ts:126–147` returns no intent for other Alt-modified keys and allows them through while holding. With a dock tab focused, open Alt+Tab, keep Alt held, and press W: the current underlying panel closes (2 tabs → 1) while the switcher stays open with another space highlighted. Likewise the list-order shortcuts can change the underlying space during the hold. **Required:** explicitly arbitrate non-switcher shortcuts while holding: consume them, or cancel/commit before routing them, so an open selection overlay cannot conceal unrelated panel mutations. Evidence: `browser-adversarial.json` → `alt-w-during-hold`. Ordinary composer typing and hold/cancel focus preservation passed separately.

## Verification

- `npm test`: **764 passed, 0 failed** (`test.log`).
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:check`: **passed** (`lint.log`, `typecheck.log`, `build.log`).
- Fresh build and archived committed dist compare byte-for-byte equal (`dist-comparison.log`, empty). Tracked node_modules files: **0**.
- Temporarily removed the `SpacesSection` preface mount in the private copy: `test/utilityRail.test.ts` changed from **5 pass** to **4 pass / 1 fail**, then returned to **5 pass** after restoring the original source (`source-guard-red.log`, `source-guard-green.log`).
- Re-ran the builder browser scenario on the private build: rail placement; unread/blocked counts; 1000ms dwell; hidden tabs; reload persistence; quick flip; hold/cycle/Shift+Tab/release; Escape; blur-event cancellation; list-order shortcuts; folded-state persistence; light/dark screenshots; no bottom-strip DOM; **all passed**, no page errors (`browser.json`, `browser-baseline.log`). Browser runs use Chromium on Linux; native macOS Option delivery was not independently tested.
- Added browser cases: rename through F2/Enter, arrow navigation, drag reorder and announcement, close/reopen space, long switcher list, and the signal/shortcut failures above (`browser-adversarial.json`).
- Added lifecycle checks: unread panel sent to a new space leaves the source count and appears in the destination; viewing clears it; closing a hidden unread panel removes the count; composer retains focus/draft during hold/cancel; legacy v1 restores its agent panel and shows the degraded status with switcher disabled. **Passed**, no page errors (`browser-lifecycle.json`).
- Sending to an existing populated destination was refused as “recovering” by unchanged `dockLayout.ts` sanitation. The source panel was retained, correctly retaining its count. This is recorded in `browser-adversarial.json`; I do not attribute that pre-existing refusal to this diff. A move to a new destination was independently successful.
- All browser scripts, logs, screenshots and the GET-only live fleet snapshot are in this evidence directory. Synthetic fleet/EventSource fixtures isolate status transitions; no live agents were messaged or driven by browser tests.

## Decisions and simplicity

- The rail move, removal of `SpaceStrip`/overflow code and CSS, versioned collapsed preference, distinct blocked styling, and accessible count labels are coherent and substantially simpler than width measurement plus overflow.
- The 1000ms dwell, preserving old markers during an active turn, blur cancellation, and quick-flip reveal delay are reasonable. Pure viewing/switcher models earn their keep; behavioral tests cover their transitions. The live region accompanies the listbox since focus stays in the workspace; scroll visibility still needs finding 4.
- The small 35-line `browserRecord` helper earns its keep for two identical last-good protocols; retain it. Its tests cover corrupt primaries and write failure.
- The read-marker cap is an eviction policy, not true LRU: viewing an unchanged marker does not touch its order. More importantly, eviction followed by seeding can forget an unread completion. Avoid deleting markers for currently open agents; this is a concrete simplification target when revisiting the signal. The 64-entry MRU cap is unnecessary for 16 live spaces if deleted IDs are pruned against live definitions; either keep the current tiny implementation or replace the arbitrary cap with that rule, without adding another model.
- MRU persistence is correct through the shared active-space effect, but it belongs with the switcher rather than `useSpaceAttention`; moving those few lines removes an unrelated dependency between unread derivation and switching.
- Existing model tests are useful, but they assume the disputed fingerprint contract instead of validating it. Add the late-vitals, placed/unplaced, equal/missing-marker and long-list cases above. No production fixes were made during review.

cat > /tmp/line-mole-fix.txt <<'EOF'
spaces-rail: visu REQUEST-CHANGES. Full report: hcom event #348613 (hcom events --sql "id=348613"); evidence under /home/ubuntu/Coding/missions/missions/fleet-refit/artifacts/spaces-rail-review/. Fix all 5 on the same branch, new commit(s):

1+2+3 (turn signal). context_used is a gauge, not a completion identity, and agent_session is missing on unplaced Rows. Replace the fingerprint with a BACKEND turn-end marker; this Go change is approved by me (the owner offered "a proper read marker to herder backend"). Shape: hcom already records every status transition as a status event with a monotonic id (`hcom events --type status`; data.old_status/new_status, instance = agent name). Add to BOTH the fleetview Row and the placed Pane JSON one field, e.g. `turn_end_id` (int64, omitempty): the id of the latest status event where that agent entered listening from a non-listening status. Compute it in the serve incrementally (an id cursor, fold new status events each refresh, keyed by agent name and reset on a new incarnation/session), never a full-history scan per poll; reuse however herder already shells hcom and its timeouts; no hcom writes. Go tests for the fold (enter listening from active counts; listening→listening doesn't; incarnation reset). Web: unread = turn_end_id > stored marker for that agent; a never-seen agent or an agent whose first turn_end_id arrives late is SEEDED silently (unknown baseline ≠ new completion — finding 2); markers follow the agent name, not placement (finding 3); no turn_end_id = never unread (blocked still shows). Add the late-marker, placed↔unplaced and missing-marker tests. Never evict markers of currently-open agents; drop the cap if it no longer earns its keep. If hcom's event store can't support this cheaply, STOP and tell me before building a workaround.
4. Switcher: scroll the highlighted option into view on reveal and on every index change (block: nearest); test with 16 spaces.
5. While the switcher is held, consume every non-switcher shortcut (Alt+W etc. and ⇧⌥←/→) so nothing mutates the workspace under the overlay; test Alt+W during hold leaves the panel count unchanged.
Also from the review: move the MRU persistence out of useSpaceAttention next to the switcher. Re-run all gates plus `go vet ./...` and `go test -count=1 ./...` in tools/herder, rebuild dist, rerun your browser proof plus visu's adversarial cases, report sha + stat + gates on thread spaces-rail.
EOF
hcom send @impl-mole --intent request --thread spaces-rail --file /tmp/line-mole-fix.txt --name line 2>&1 | tail -1

content.text:
<status>spaces-rail is on a fix round: the reviewer asked for 5 changes, and mole is working on them, including a small backend change.</status>

I've made one design call for spaces-rail, since you had offered the backend option. The reviewer proved that the page can't tell reliably when an agent finishes a turn. It was inferring that from the context-size number, which doesn't always change between turns. The number also fires false "waiting" markers when an agent is moved between placed and unplaced, or when its stats arrive late.

hcom already logs every status change with an increasing id. So mole is adding one field to herder's fleet data: the id of the agent's most recent "finished a turn and is now waiting" event. The page compares that id against what you've already viewed. Nothing is written back to hcom.

Mole is also fixing two switcher problems the reviewer found:
- With a long list of spaces, the highlight could scroll out of view.
- Other ⌥ shortcuts, such as ⌥W, could still close a panel underneath the switcher while it was open.

The reviewer, visu, stays up to re-check the fixes.
